items.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR12 reservation ("def operational model/data/calibration/uncertainty vocabulary"); prose-scaffold.md SR12 row ("All four secondary narratives, exact report destinations above; no primary experiment source")
items.design_state: explicit-definition-contract; formulation vocabulary only, no measurement, no sampling law and no statistical inference
items.physical_scope: Formulation vocabulary inside the flat special-relativity framework: it names run descriptions, operational models, data records, calibration declarations and uncertainty bounds built from the framework's own objects (events, worldlines, clocks, observers, ideal waves, radar readings, observer energies and frequencies) and its SI conventions. It asserts no measurement, no apparatus behaviour, no realized experiment, no sampling law, no statistical inference and no value of any physical constant; in particular it does not claim that any laboratory realizes an operational model.
items.statement:
Adopt the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], the ideal-clock and ideal-light assumptions of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], the ideal plane-wave and frequency-reading model of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]], the operational radar protocol of [[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]], the massive-particle measurement identification of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] clause (ii) and the massless-particle measurement identification of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] clause (ii). This definition introduces the framework's experimental-interface vocabulary; it selects no experiment, records no value and asserts no comparison.

**(a) Run descriptions.** A *run description* is a finite tuple $D=(d_1,\dots,d_r)$ whose entries are framework objects of the following kinds, each declared with its domain and regularity as specified by the cited item, together with the frame, observer, event or unit convention required for a numerical reading where such a reading is used: a point of the affine Minkowski space $A$ (an event, [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]); a vector of $V$ of declared causal character ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); a future timelike worldline together with its proper-time function ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[def-sr-proper-time]]); a future unit timelike vector or a smooth observer congruence ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]); a future null wave covector with its affine phase ([[def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector]]); a radar time or radar distance assigned by the operational radar protocol ([[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]]); an observer angular frequency ([[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]]); an observer energy, spatial momentum, kinetic energy or invariant mass ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]); and a real parameter vector in a declared subset of $\mathbb R^m$ with declared units. A run description is a description of a model configuration; the tuple asserts nothing about any apparatus or about nature.

**(b) Operational model.** An *operational model* is a tuple $M=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ in which: $S$ is a nonempty set, the *preparation index set*; $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is a nonempty *parameter set* and $\theta:S\to\Theta$ is a surjection, the *parameter map*; $D$ assigns to each $s\in S$ a run description $D(s)$ of (a); and for some integer $d\ge1$ the map $F:\Theta\to\mathbb R^d$ is a *prediction map* for $D$, subject to the declared interpretation $(*)$: for every $s\in S$, each component of $F(\theta(s))$ is a number that the framework's definitions, postulates and proved consequences assign to the description $D(s)$, with every intermediate quantity, frame, event, sign and unit declared. A pair $(M,F)$ is called an operational model for the quantity whose values $F$ computes. Condition $(*)$ is a declared interpretation that reviewers check when the model is used; it is not a consequence of the tuple structure, and no clause of this definition asserts that any apparatus realizes $M$ or that $F(\theta(s))$ is measured.

**(c) Data records.** A *data record* is a tuple $R=(N,z,\varepsilon,a)$ with an integer $N\ge1$; $z=(z_1,\dots,z_N)$ with $z_k\in\mathbb R^d$; $\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_N)$ with $\varepsilon_k\in[0,\infty)^d$; and $a=(a_1,\dots,a_N)$ a finite tuple of *condition annotations*, each a finite string identifying the declared run condition of the datum and, when the datum is taken from a report, the bibliographic identification of that report. The record declares: for each $k$, the value of the quantity of (b) under the condition annotated by $a_k$ lies in the closed box $\prod_{j=1}^d[z_{k,j}-\varepsilon_{k,j},\,z_{k,j}+\varepsilon_{k,j}]$, in the declared units. A data record contains no probability space, random variable, distribution, sampling law, independence assumption, likelihood or coverage statement; it declares nothing about how the values $z_k$ were produced and nothing about the correctness of any calibration.

**(d) Calibration declarations.** Let $Z$ be a nonempty set of declared *instrument-output values*. A *calibration declaration* is a tuple $C=(Z,c,\delta,h)$ with $c:Z\to\mathbb R^d$, $\delta:Z\to[0,\infty)^d$ and $h$ a condition annotation; it declares that for every $z\in Z$ obtained under the condition annotated by $h$, the value of the declared quantity lies in the closed box $\prod_j[c_j(z)-\delta_j(z),\,c_j(z)+\delta_j(z)]$ in the declared units. A *calibration record* is a data record of (c) whose declared quantity is the value of the calibration map's output. The declaration asserts no accuracy beyond the bound $\delta$ and no statistical property of $c$ or $\delta$.

**(e) Uncertainty vocabulary.** For a data record of (c), the *declared uncertainty* of the $k$-th datum is the vector $\varepsilon_k$; a *source label* is an element of the finite declared set $\{\text{calibration},\ \text{systematic},\ \text{sampling-variability},\ \text{rounding},\ \text{other}\}$ attached to a bound; and a *total declared bound* for a value computed from finitely many recorded values by a declared finite arithmetic expression is any $B\in[0,\infty)$ for which the declaration states: whenever each recorded value lies in its declared closed box, the computed value lies in $[\hat y-B,\hat y+B]$ for the declared number $\hat y$ (for instance, for a sum of recorded scalars the sum of the recorded bounds is such a bound). Every uncertainty entry is a declared constraint of the form in (c) and (d); no probability law, coverage probability, confidence level, p-value or posterior is defined by this vocabulary.

**(f) Comparison claims are separate.** A claim that a data record $R$ and an operational model $M$ are consistent, or that $R$ supports, refutes or fails to distinguish $M$, is not part of (a)-(e): it requires its own statement, an explicitly declared comparison rule and adequate primary-report and analysis prerequisites. For the current stored-lithium-ion optical Doppler report, that research prerequisite, labelled M20 in the source design, is supplied by `exp-sr-stored-lithium-ion-doppler-time-dilation-2014` and `pthm-sr-specified-model-comparison`. The comparison theorem distinguishes hard-bound records of (c) from separately defined source-reported estimates and standard-uncertainty scales; the latter are not hard bounds or coverage guarantees. It permits comparison with specified alternative prediction hypotheses, which are not thereby operational models of the SR framework and are not asserted to satisfy condition $(*)$ in (b). Other primary-report families remain subject to their own retrieval and analysis obligations. These are nonlogical status pointers to the separate empirical record and comparison claim; no clause of this vocabulary licenses a conclusion about the truth of a postulate or of the framework.

**(g) Well-definedness and scope.** All components of (a)-(e) are finite tuples of sets, maps and real numbers with declared domains and units; the constructions use no choice principle and no measurability, integrability, completeness or differentiability beyond the cited items, and clause (b) evaluates a prediction only at parameter values for which the cited items supply its ingredients. The vocabulary asserts no measurement, no apparatus behaviour, no empirical support or refutation, no value of the constant $c$ or of any other physical parameter, and no statistical inference.
items.strategy: A definition item. Well-definedness: (a) enumerates object kinds each supplied by a cited item with its own domain and regularity, and requires the reading conventions to be declared rather than inferred; (b) is a tuple of a set, a subset of $\mathbb R^m$, two maps and a finite tuple, all of them finite data with declared domains; the map $F$ is evaluated only at the parameter values $\theta(s)$ for which the cited items define its ingredients; (c) and (d) are finite tuples of real vectors, nonnegative bounds and annotation strings, so each closed box $\prod_j[z_j-\varepsilon_j,z_j+\varepsilon_j]$ is a well-defined subset of $\mathbb R^d$ because $\varepsilon_j\ge0$; (e) defines the declared-bound vocabulary by a stated property rather than by an extremal or optimality claim, and (f) states the separateness of comparison claims. Condition $(*)$ of (b) is deliberately an interpretation obligation: the definition names the tuple and its intended reading, and any use of an operational model must check $(*)$ against the specific framework items (for the Doppler instance of this page, [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] supplies it). No choice principle is used anywhere: all constructions are finite tuples and pointwise evaluations. The scope clauses exclude measurements, apparatus behaviour, calibration correctness and all statistical notions; the reader should note that an operational model is a mathematical structure of the framework and not a claim that any laboratory realizes it.

items.physical_scope: Scope declaration of the framework's empirical interface: it records a research queue of primary-report destinations and the qualifications future experiment items must carry. It asserts no measurement, no dataset, no uncertainty value, no comparison result, no deviation, no empirical support for any postulate and no precision of any physical constant.
items.statement:
Scope-and-queue record for the empirical layer of the flat special-relativity framework, stated in the vocabulary of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]].

(i) The actual primary Botermann et al.2014 stored-lithium-ion Ives-Stilwell report has now been retrieved and read in full. The proposed experiment records its apparatus,calibration,finite sampling,frequency estimates and1sigma budget; the comparison theorem supplies explicit conditional bound and reported-scale analysis. No raw dataset or new coverage claim is supplied.

(ii) The source design declares four *primary-report search destinations* for future experiment items of this framework. Each is named here as a destination, that is, a family of published reports to retrieve and read in full text, and none of them is evidence for any postulate: (a) historical ether and light-propagation experiments (interferometric or resonance tests of the constancy of the coordinate speed of light between inertial charts, and Doppler-shift tests of moving emitters); (b) unstable-particle lifetime measurements (beam or storage-ring measurements of a particle's lifetime at a measured speed compared with its lifetime at rest); (c) accelerator kinematics of charged particles at high Lorentz factor (measurements of momentum, energy or speed relating a particle's measured quantities to its velocity); (d) clock-transport and clock-comparison experiments (aircraft-, satellite- or laboratory-borne atomic clocks comparing the elapsed times of differently moving or differently situated ideal clocks). The secondary narratives consulted for this page mention instances of these families, among them the historical ether-and-Maxwell context (Crowell pp. 13-15), the 1938 Ives-Stilwell Doppler test (Crowell p. 57), storage-ring muon-lifetime measurements (Crowell pp. 28-29), the 1971 Hafele-Keating aircraft atomic-clock comparison (Crowell pp. 15, 26, 28; Tong pp. 24-25) and a 2010 low-speed atomic-clock measurement (Crowell p. 28); those mentions are contextual motivation only and are not documentation of reported measurements here.

(iii) Before any experiment item can be authored on a destination, the actual primary report must be retrieved and read, and the record must carry the apparatus and preparation, operational definitions of the measured quantities, the calibration model, the sampling and error model, the treatment of systematic errors, the measured values with their reported uncertainties, and the source's limitations. Textbook and review narratives are not substitutes for the primary reports.

(iv) The comparison of model predictions with recorded data is a separate promised physics-theorem obligation which the source design declares to require the primary-report and analysis layer (research label M20); that layer is now supplied for the specified2014 stored-lithium-ion report by the experiment and comparison theorem, while the other primary-report families remain research queues.

(v) Qualifications any future comparison must carry: observations test the combined model and apparatus assumptions; finite-sample agreement does not establish a postulate or a model; a p-value would not be the probability that a theory is false and a confidence level would not be a posterior probability; and a finite bounded record does not by itself determine a unique parameter or adjudicate between distinct models.

(vi) This remark is a queue/status pointer; measured estimates and their qualifications are recorded only in the experiment item. It supplies no independent empirical conclusion or certainty.

The four-family search queue remains intact: this single optical Doppler primary report supplies one branch of family(a); historical ether/interferometer reports and the lifetime,accelerator and transported-clock families still require actual retrieval and reading. Source-cited RMS/SME analyses remain separate queue obligations.

Current nonlogical status pointers: `exp-sr-stored-lithium-ion-doppler-time-dilation-2014` records the primary observations; `pthm-sr-specified-model-comparison` gives the separate conditional comparison. These pointers add no logical prerequisite.
items.strategy: This is a scope-and-queue remark. Its current status is that the full Botermann et al. (2014) primary report has been retrieved and read, the same-page experiment proposal records its qualified observations, and `pthm-sr-specified-model-comparison` supplies complete finite calibrated-bound and reported-scale comparison rules with a faithful report instantiation. The research label M20 is therefore supplied for this specified optical Doppler report. It is not an unresolved global requirement for this comparison, and it is not certification of the remaining report families. Clause (ii) preserves all four original search destinations and identifies textbook narratives as contextual motivation only. Clause (iii) retains the apparatus, preparation, operational definition, calibration, finite sampling, systematic-error, observation and limitation requirements for future reports. Clause (v) preserves the distinction between conditional model comparison and empirical certainty. The source's raw spectra, fit weights and covariance are not supplied or invented; its standard uncertainties are not hard bounds or coverage guarantees. This remark provides nonlogical status pointers to `exp-sr-stored-lithium-ion-doppler-time-dilation-2014` and `pthm-sr-specified-model-comparison`; it does not supply either item's proof or empirical premise. No dependency cycle is introduced, and no original source-harvest or queue history is removed.

items.physical_scope: Primary report of optical-optical double resonance spectroscopy of stored metastable 7Li+ ions in the ESR interaction section, with nominal speed beta = 0.338, calibrated laser frequencies, active-transition invariance and resonance-model auxiliaries. Describes a measured estimate and source-labelled standard uncertainty, not exact frequencies, a hard true-value bound, guaranteed coverage, raw data, or validation of every SR postulate. Atomic spectroscopy, real line widths, beam dynamics and calibration are empirical apparatus auxiliaries, not deductions from the ideal-plane-wave postulate.
items.setup:
**Quantities and apparatus notation.** The laboratory speed parameter is $ eta=v/c$, with $v$ the selected ion-class speed in an approximately inertial laboratory description; its quoted value is nominal. Frequencies $
u_1,
u_2,
u_p,
u_a>0$ are scalar estimates in hertz of the two rest transitions and the parallel/antiparallel laser readings, respectively; the ideal-model convention is $
u=\omega/(2\pi)$ and $\lambda=c/
u$ from [[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]], while the real apparatus has finite-width spectra. Here $\mathrm{MHz}=10^6\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, $\mathrm{nm}=10^{-9}\,\mathrm m$, and $\mu\mathrm{rad}=10^{-6}$ radians. For a single-peaked nonnegative profile, its full width at half maximum (FWHM) is the separation of the two frequencies (or speeds) at half its peak height, when those crossings exist; the reported $\delta v/v$ uses the speed width divided by the selected speed. Beam divergence and alignment are angles between ion trajectories and the specified beam axis. A Lambda system here means three source-labelled atomic levels, two lower and one common upper, with the two listed driven transitions; the symbols $3S_1$, $3P_2$ and $F$ distinguish the report's atomic levels, rather than supplying a quantum-state model. Metastable lifetime means the reported characteristic persistence time of the prepared level; no survival distribution is inferred. The Penning source, ESR (Experimental Storage Ring), electron cooling, lasers and optics below are the report's named preparation and control apparatus; their performance is reported empirically, not derived from SR. The energy label $\mathrm{MeV/u}$ is energy per atomic-mass unit: $1\,\mathrm{MeV}=10^6$ electronvolts, with one electronvolt the energy acquired by elementary charge across one volt; it is not used here to deduce the nominal speed.

The experiment used $^7\mathrm{Li}^+$ ions from a Penning ion gauge source, accelerated to $58.6\,\mathrm{MeV/u}$ and stored in the ESR at nominal $ eta=0.338$. Electron cooling reduced the reported longitudinal velocity spread to $\delta v/v\approx9	imes10^{-6}$ (FWHM) and transverse divergence to less than $100\,\mu\mathrm{rad}$. About $10^7$ to $10^8$ ions were stored, with an estimated metastable fraction below $1\%$. The metastable $3S_1$ lifetime was $15$–$30\,\mathrm{s}$ in the ring, compared with $50\,\mathrm{s}$ in vacuum. The Lambda system used the transitions $3S_1(F=3/2)	o3P_2(F=5/2)$ and $3S_1(F=5/2)	o3P_2(F=5/2)$. Parallel and antiparallel beams near $386\,\mathrm{nm}$ and $780\,\mathrm{nm}$ addressed its two legs; an additional $780\,\mathrm{nm}$ beam repumped ions into the system.
items.procedure:
**Count and fit objects.** A spectrum in this account is a finite list of frequency settings $f_i\in\mathbb R$ with detected pulse counts $n_{i,h}\in\mathbb N_0$ in each switching configuration $h\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and window. Fluorescence denotes the emitted light counted by the photomultipliers; a dark count is a registered pulse without applied excitation. Subtracted or averaged spectra are real-valued lists, not nonnegative integer counts or independent trials. A Lorentzian peak plus linear background means a fitted function $L:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of the form $L(f)=A/[1+4(f-f_0)^2/w^2]+b_0+b_1(f-f_0)$ with $A>0$, $w>0$; $f_0,w$ have frequency units, and the peak term has half height at $f_0\pm w/2$. Residuals are the differences of processed values and the fitted values at the recorded settings. A weighted average of fitted centers has form $\sum_i w_i f_{0,i}/\sum_i w_i$ for nonnegative weights with positive sum; the report does not give the weights or their construction. Frequency locking means controlling a laser reading relative to a specified reference or offset; second-harmonic generation denotes conversion to twice the optical frequency. Optical-optical double resonance is the selected condition that both listed transitions are resonant for the same ion velocity class; it is an apparatus selection model, not a measured probability law.

The parallel beam was generated by doubling a $772\,\mathrm{nm}$ Ti:Sa laser locked to an iodine marker previously calibrated with a frequency comb against a rubidium clock. The antiparallel diode laser was offset-locked to a rubidium reference, with a $600\,\mathrm{MHz}$ tuning range. Polarization-maintaining fibers transported the beams. Motorized stages controlled angles and positions to $20\,\mu\mathrm{rad}$ and $50\,\mu\mathrm{m}$; scrapers established laser/ion overlap within $80\,\mu\mathrm{rad}$. Photomultipliers counted fluorescence in four successive $100\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ configurations: both excitation beams, antiparallel only, parallel only, and neither. Dark counts were subtracted, then the separate-beam background was subtracted from the both-beam spectrum. Optical-optical double resonance selected ions for which both Lambda legs were resonant at the same velocity. To compensate metastable depletion, an $81$-point scan was paused after $69$ points for injection and cooling. Figure 2 shows an example averaged over $44$ scans, with $49\,\mathrm{MHz}$ laboratory linewidth and $35\,\mathrm{MHz}$ rest-frame linewidth. The authors fitted $40$ spectra with Lorentzians on linear backgrounds and formed a weighted average. Raw count tables, fit weights, a covariance matrix and a complete likelihood are not published in this report.

items.uncertainty:
The Gouy phase is the additional spatial phase of a focused beam relative to a plane-wave phase; for a $C^1$ phase correction $\psi:J\to\mathbb R$ on a proper-time interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, the phase-reading convention assigns a frequency correction $-(2\pi)^{-1}d\psi/d\tau$ under the stipulated phase-reading interpretation. No beam profile $\psi$ is reconstructed here. The $1\sigma$ notation below is the source\'s label for an uncertainty scale; without its full estimation model it specifies neither a guaranteed interval nor a sampling distribution.

Table I labels its uncertainties $1\sigma$. In MHz, the aggregate entries are $0.43$ for each rest frequency, $1.6$ for the antiparallel frequency and $1.25$ for the parallel frequency. Antiparallel contributions are: weighted-fit statistical uncertainty $0.6$, rubidium reference $0.05$, diode stabilization $0.64$, background linearization $0.5$, Gouy phase $1.0$, angular alignment $0.6$, and ion divergence $0.4$. Parallel contributions are: iodine reference $0.06$, Ti:Sa stabilization $0.12$, Gouy phase $1.0$, alignment $0.6$, and divergence $0.4$. The inferred Gouy correction for each laser was $0.44\pm1.0\,\mathrm{MHz}$, from experimentally validated numerical simulation using measured beam parameters. The authors reported no significant residual asymmetry; simulated background linearization was assigned $0.5\,\mathrm{MHz}$. The excess linewidth, about five times the expected width, was attributed mainly to drift-induced fluorescence. The $0.6\,\mathrm{MHz}$ statistical entry comes from the weighted analysis of forty fitted spectra, not forty independent raw clock readings. These reported statistical and systematic scales are preserved without inventing independence, a Gaussian total sampling law, fit weights, covariance or coverage.
items.interpretation: The measured observable tests the combined Doppler/time-dilation, active atomic-transition and vacuum-wave invariance assumptions together with resonance selection, calibration, beam alignment and correction models. The source reports no resolved deviation at its uncertainty level and quotes $|\alpha|\le2.0\times10^{-8}$ for $\alpha=\epsilon/\beta^2$. That quotation is recorded as the source's test-theory sensitivity statement, rather than a newly certified hard bound or confidence interval. RMS and SME parameter translations and future higher-boost prospects remain contextual research topics; they are not prerequisites or claims of the comparison theorem.

empirical_result.observation: Reported epsilon = (1.5 +/- 2.3) x 10^-9, source equation (4), with 1-sigma budget in Table I.
empirical_result.uncertainty: Reported u_epsilon = 2.3 x 10^-9; includes fitting, calibration, background, Gouy-phase, alignment and divergence uncertainty scales; no probability or coverage guaranteed.
empirical_result.conditions: Stored 7Li+ ESR optical-optical double resonance experiment at nominal beta = 0.338; Table I laser and rest-frequency inputs, same-velocity Lambda resonance, source correction and calibration models and active-invariance auxiliary assumptions.

The energy label $\mathrm{MeV/u}$ is energy per atomic-mass unit: $1\,\mathrm{MeV}=10^6$ electronvolts, with one electronvolt the energy acquired by elementary charge across one volt; it is not used here to deduce the nominal speed.

The experiment used $^7\mathrm{Li}^+$ ions from a Penning ion gauge source, accelerated to $58.6\,\mathrm{MeV/u}$ and stored in the ESR at nominal $\beta=0.338$. The metastable $3S_1$ lifetime was $15$–$30\,\mathrm{s}$ in the ring, compared with $50\,\mathrm{s}$ in vacuum. The Lambda system used the transitions $3S_1(F=3/2)\to3P_2(F=5/2)$ and $3S_1(F=5/2)\to3P_2(F=5/2)$. Parallel and antiparallel beams near $386\,\mathrm{nm}$ and $780\,\mathrm{nm}$ addressed its two legs; an additional $780\,\mathrm{nm}$ beam repumped ions into the system.

## Procedure

**Count and fit objects.** A spectrum in this account is a finite list of frequency settings $f_i\in\mathbb R$ with detected pulse counts $n_{i,h}\in\mathbb N_0$ in each switching configuration $h\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and window. Fluorescence denotes the emitted light counted by the photomultipliers; a dark count is a registered pulse without applied excitation. Subtracted or averaged spectra are real-valued lists, not nonnegative integer counts or independent trials. Residuals are the differences of processed values and the fitted values at the recorded settings. A weighted average of fitted centers has form $\sum_i w_i f_{0,i}/\sum_i w_i$ for nonnegative weights with positive sum; the report does not give the weights or their construction. Frequency locking means controlling a laser reading relative to a specified reference or offset; second-harmonic generation denotes conversion to twice the optical frequency. Optical-optical double resonance is the selected condition that both listed transitions are resonant for the same ion velocity class; it is an apparatus selection model, not a measured probability law.

The parallel beam was generated by doubling a $772\,\mathrm{nm}$ Ti:Sa laser locked to an iodine marker previously calibrated with a frequency comb against a rubidium clock. The antiparallel diode laser was offset-locked to a rubidium reference, with a $600\,\mathrm{MHz}$ tuning range. Polarization-maintaining fibers transported the beams. Motorized stages controlled angles and positions to $20\,\mu\mathrm{rad}$ and $50\,\mu\mathrm{m}$; scrapers established laser/ion overlap within $80\,\mu\mathrm{rad}$. Photomultipliers counted fluorescence in four successive $100\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ configurations: both excitation beams, antiparallel only, parallel only, and neither. Dark counts were subtracted, then the separate-beam background was subtracted from the both-beam spectrum. Optical-optical double resonance selected ions for which both Lambda legs were resonant at the same velocity. To compensate metastable depletion, an $81$-point scan was paused after $69$ points for injection and cooling. Figure 2 shows an example averaged over $44$ scans, with $49\,\mathrm{MHz}$ laboratory linewidth and $35\,\mathrm{MHz}$ rest-frame linewidth. The authors fitted $40$ spectra with Lorentzians on linear backgrounds and formed a weighted average. Raw count tables, fit weights, a covariance matrix and a complete likelihood are not published in this report.

## Observations

Table I gives the frequency estimates, in MHz, $\nu_1=546455143.0$, $\nu_2=546474960.7$, $\nu_a=384225534.98$ and $\nu_p=777210326.98$. The rest-frame inputs $\nu_1,\nu_2$ come from earlier measurements cited as references 21–22; those papers were not retrieved or read here. Equation (4) reports $\epsilon=\sqrt{\nu_a\nu_p/(\nu_1\nu_2)}-1=(1.5\pm2.3)\times10^{-9}$ at nominal $\beta=0.338$. These are estimates with the source-labelled $1\sigma$ uncertainty budget, not exact values or guaranteed bounds. The rounded Table I centers yield approximately $1.4744849565\times10^{-9}$, consistent with the reported rounded estimate, without reconstructing unrounded data.

## Uncertainty

The Gouy phase is the additional spatial phase of a focused beam relative to a plane-wave phase; for a $C^1$ phase correction $\psi:J\to\mathbb R$ on a proper-time interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, the phase-reading convention assigns a frequency correction $-(2\pi)^{-1}d\psi/d\tau$ under the stipulated phase-reading interpretation. No beam profile $\psi$ is reconstructed here. The $1\sigma$ notation below is the source\'s label for an uncertainty scale; without its full estimation model it specifies neither a guaranteed interval nor a sampling distribution.

Table I labels its uncertainties $1\sigma$. In MHz, the aggregate entries are $0.43$ for each rest frequency, $1.6$ for the antiparallel frequency and $1.25$ for the parallel frequency. Antiparallel contributions are: weighted-fit statistical uncertainty $0.6$, rubidium reference $0.05$, diode stabilization $0.64$, background linearization $0.5$, Gouy phase $1.0$, angular alignment $0.6$, and ion divergence $0.4$. Parallel contributions are: iodine reference $0.06$, Ti:Sa stabilization $0.12$, Gouy phase $1.0$, alignment $0.6$, and divergence $0.4$. The inferred Gouy correction for each laser was $0.44\pm1.0\,\mathrm{MHz}$, from experimentally validated numerical simulation using measured beam parameters. The authors reported no significant residual asymmetry; simulated background linearization was assigned $0.5\,\mathrm{MHz}$. The excess linewidth, about five times the expected width, was attributed mainly to drift-induced fluorescence. The $0.6\,\mathrm{MHz}$ statistical entry comes from the weighted analysis of forty fitted spectra, not forty independent raw clock readings. These reported statistical and systematic scales are preserved without inventing independence, a Gaussian total sampling law, fit weights, covariance or coverage.

## Interpretation

The measured observable tests the combined Doppler/time-dilation, active atomic-transition and vacuum-wave invariance assumptions together with resonance selection, calibration, beam alignment and correction models. The source reports no resolved deviation at its uncertainty level and quotes $|\alpha|\le2.0\times10^{-8}$ for $\alpha=\epsilon/\beta^2$. That quotation is recorded as the source's test-theory sensitivity statement, rather than a newly certified hard bound or confidence interval. RMS and SME parameter translations and future higher-boost prospects remain contextual research topics; they are not prerequisites or claims of the comparison theorem.

items.statement:
Adopt [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]]. Comparison labels below range over explicitly specified prediction hypotheses, each with its own apparatus and calibration assumptions. When a label is an operational model of the SR framework, its prediction map must satisfy clause (b), condition $(*)$, of that vocabulary using the specified SR suppliers. A competing prediction hypothesis need not be an SR operational model and is not represented as satisfying $(*)$. Reported standard uncertainties are a separate record type, not the vocabulary's declared hard-bound records.

**(a) General finite comparison.** An apparatus/calibration nuisance parameter means an additional declared model input constrained together with the physical parameter; its domain is part of the admissible set below, and no probability law is implicit. Flatten a finite $d$-dimensional record with $N$ entries to $m=Nd$ real coordinates. For each label $\ell$, let $A_\ell$ be a declared set of admissible tuples $a=(	heta,\eta,b)$, where $	heta$ is a physical parameter, $\eta$ an apparatus or calibration nuisance parameter, and $b\in\mathbb R^m$ an additive calibration correction. Let $P_\ell:A_\ell	o\mathbb R^m$ be its corrected prediction, $P_\ell(a)=F_\ell(	heta,\eta)+b$; every correction and admissibility constraint is explicitly stated. For a declared hard-bound record $(z,e)$ put $B(z,e)=\prod_{j=1}^m[z_j-e_j,z_j+e_j]$ and $C_\ell=\{a\in A_\ell:P_\ell(a)\in B(z,e)\}$. Then $C_\ell

If every prediction in $P_\ell(A_\ell)$ has coordinate $j$ in $[L_j,U_j]$ disjoint from $[z_j-e_j,z_j+e_j]$, then $C_\ell=\varnothing$. **(d) Primary-report instantiation.** Under the qualified conditions of `exp-sr-stored-lithium-ion-doppler-time-dilation-2014`, additionally stipulate that resonance identifies each laser frequency in the ions' instantaneous rest frame with its stated rest transition frequency, that those transition frequencies are unchanged under active boosts, and that the ideal vacuum phase and frequency law applies in the interaction section after the report's beam, Gouy-phase and line-shape corrections. items.strategy:
The proof below uses $\nu_a=a$, $\nu_p=p$, $\nu_1=r_1$, $\nu_2=r_2$ when abbreviating the four frequencies; candidate labels include explicitly alternative prediction hypotheses as well as SR operational models. Only the SR member is required and shown to satisfy vocabulary condition $(*)$. 1.1 By definition C_l is the preimage of B under P_l; existence of a in C_l is precisely existence of a in A_l with P_l(a) in B, equivalent to nonempty intersection of the image with B. Under the declared true-value/bound and candidate assumptions, that specified a belongs to C_l. If C_l is empty the conjunction is impossible, with no claim about which premise fails. [given]
1.2 If every candidate coordinate j lies in [L_j,U_j] disjoint from its data interval, no prediction lies in the product B. Thus C_l is empty. The criterion is sufficient only: for example the prediction set {(0,1),(1,0)} has both coordinate projections overlapping the box {(0,0)}, yet the intersection is empty. Calibration/nuisance constraints are retained inside A_l and cannot be discarded by replacing a joint feasible set with its marginal projections. [step 1.1]
2.1 In the positive frequency rectangle, multiplying positive intervals increases numerator bounds and division by positive denominator reverses denominator extrema, by sign rules. The increasing positive square root preserves these inequalities. Hence the stated lower/upper Q bounds hold. The corner a_minus,p_minus,r1_plus,r2_plus attains the lower value, and the opposite corner the upper value. This uses only the stated rectangular hard-bound domain, not a probabilistic interpretation of standard uncertainties. [given]
3.1 Because u_j>0, abs(zhat_j-P_j)<=k*u_j is exactly zhat_j-k*u_j<=P_j<=zhat_j+k*u_j. A finite maximum is <=k exactly when every coordinate ratio is <=k. Intersecting these constraints proves the asserted scale-consistency preimage identity. It is arithmetic of fixed real estimates and scales, with no random variable or probability measure, so it supplies no statistical rejection/coverage conclusion. [given]
4.1 Apply the existing SR Doppler result separately to the parallel and antiparallel ideal waves and the instantaneous rest observer beta e1. Linear rather than angular frequencies share the factors because division by2pi cancels. With the explicitly stipulated resonance/active-transition auxiliaries this gives r1=gamma(1-beta)p and r2=gamma(1+beta)a. Multiply, obtaining ap/(r1r2)=1/(gamma^2(1-beta^2))=1; positive square root gives Q_SR=0. Replacing the stipulated common factor by Gamma=1 gives Q_1=1/sqrt(1-beta^2)-1. The SR supplier proves only the ideal transformation, not the atomic or line-width premises. [given]
4.2 The source estimate/scale pair gives abs(1.5e-9)/2.3e-9=15/23 and endpoints1.5e-9±2.3e-9=(-.8,3.8)e-9. For beta=169/500,1-beta^2=221439/250000. The exact positive-square comparisons (531/500)^2*(221439/250000)<1<(1063/1000)^2*(221439/250000) prove1.062<1/sqrt(1-beta^2)<1.063 by order and rational-power laws. Hence Q_1>.062 and (Q_1-1.5e-9)/(2.3e-9)>10^7, since .062-1.5e-9>.023=10^7*2.3e-9. Thus the respective k=1 classifications follow from3.1. No count model, covariance or exact speed-calibration claim enters this arithmetic. [step 3.1, step 4.1]

The experiment's apparatus, finite sampling, corrections, borrowed rest frequencies and unresolved distribution/correlation details carry through this conditional comparison. No choice principle or unproved statistical theorem is used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2]

items.statement:
Adopt the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], the vocabulary of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]] and the ideal plane-wave model of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]. Consider the longitudinal configuration of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]]: inertial charts $x$ and $x'$ whose transition is $x'=B(\beta e_1)\,x$ for a real $\beta\in(-1,1)$, where $B(\cdot)$ is the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]], so that the frame $x'$ moves with velocity $c\beta e_1$ relative to $x$; an ideal emitter history, meaning the $C^\infty$ rest worldline $h:\mathbb R\to A$, $h(\rho)=o+\rho e_0$, with length parameter $\rho$, future unit tangent $e_0$ and proper-time function $\tau_h(\rho)=\rho/c$ based at $0$ (no emission dynamics is stipulated); an ideal plane wave whose frame-$x$ data are $(\omega,s)$ with angular frequency $\omega>0$ and $s=e_1$; and the rest observer of $x'$, whose four-velocity is $c f_0$ for the future unit timelike vector $f_0$ constructed below. By clauses (i) and (ii) of that theorem this observer reads $\omega_o(\beta)=\gamma_\beta(1-\beta)\omega$ with $\gamma_\beta=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, so the *Doppler ratio* is

$$F(\beta):=\frac{\omega_o(\beta)}{\omega}=\sqrt{\frac{1-\beta}{1+\beta}},\qquad \beta\in(-1,1),$$

the rational power being that of [[def-rational-power]].

(a) Let $S:=\Theta:=(-1,1)$, $\theta:=\mathrm{id}$, let $D(\beta)$ be the run description comprising the inertial charts $x$ and $x'$, the emitter's straight rest curve, the future null wave covector with frame-$x$ data $(\omega,e_1)$ and its affine phase, its proper-time function $\tau_h$, and the observer's rest vector $f_0$ with reception event $o$, and let $F$ be as displayed. Then $M:=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ is an operational model for the dimensionless ratio $\omega_o/\omega$ in the sense of clause (b) of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]]: condition $(*)$ holds with the prediction supplied by the cited Doppler theorem, and $d=1$. The map $F$ is strictly decreasing on $(-1,1)$, and for every real $r>0$ there is exactly one $\beta\in(-1,1)$ with $F(\beta)=r$, namely

$$\beta(r)=\frac{1-r^2}{1+r^2};$$

consequently $F$ is a strictly decreasing bijection of $(-1,1)$ onto $(0,\infty)$.

(b) Let $z\in(0,1]$ and $\varepsilon\in[0,z)$ be real, so that $0<z-\varepsilon\le z+\varepsilon$, and let $R$ be the declared one-point record with $N=1$, $z_1=z$, $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon$ and condition annotation "longitudinal Doppler ratio of the moving observer in the propagation direction" in the sense of clause (c) of the vocabulary. Then the set of parameters consistent with $R$ and $M$,

$$C(R,M):=\{\beta\in(-1,1):F(\beta)\in[z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon]\},$$

equals the closed interval $[\beta(z+\varepsilon),\beta(z-\varepsilon)]$; it is nonempty, and every element of it satisfies the declared bound of $R$. If $\varepsilon=0$, it is the singleton $\{\beta(z)\}$. If $\varepsilon>0$, its endpoints are strictly ordered and its exact positive length is

$$\beta(z-\varepsilon)-\beta(z+\varepsilon)=\frac{8z\varepsilon}{[1+(z-\varepsilon)^2][1+(z+\varepsilon)^2]}>0.$$

Thus the strict inequality between the record endpoints and the positive-length conclusion apply exactly when the declared uncertainty is positive.

(c) Illustrative instance (declared illustrative values, not a measurement report): $z=9/10$ and $\varepsilon=1/100$. Then $\beta(91/100)=1719/18281\approx0.094032$ and $\beta(89/100)=2079/17921\approx0.116009$, and $C(R,M)=[1719/18281,\ 2079/17921]$, an interval of exact length $7200000/327613801$ in $\beta$, whose endpoints satisfy $F(1719/18281)=91/100$ and $F(2079/17921)=89/100$.

(d) Scope. Every number in (c) is a declared illustrative value supplied to instantiate the vocabulary's clauses and their arithmetic; the example asserts no apparatus, no calibration correctness, no measurement, no sampling model, no statistical inference and no empirical support or refutation of the Doppler theorem or of any postulate.
items.strategy:
Direct verification of each clause. (a) Condition $(*)$: the ratio $\omega_o/\omega$ for the fixed configuration $(\beta e_1,\ s=e_1)$ is read by the rest observer of $x'$ as $\gamma_\beta(1-\beta)$ by clause (ii) of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] with $\beta\cdot s=\beta$ and $|\beta|<1$; since $1-\beta>0$ and $1+\beta>0$ for $\beta\in(-1,1)$, the identity $\gamma_\beta(1-\beta)=\sqrt{(1-\beta)/(1+\beta)}$ is an elementary consequence of the rational-power laws [[lem-rational-power-laws]] and of the positivity of the square root, with the sign chosen positive. Strict decrease: for $-1<\beta_1<\beta_2<1$, the difference of the squared ratios is $2(\beta_2-\beta_1)/[(1+\beta_1)(1+\beta_2)]>0$, since both denominator factors are positive ([[lem-of-sign-rules]]); composing with the strictly increasing square-root map ([[lem-rational-power-monotone]], claim 2 with $r=1/2$) gives $F(\beta_1)>F(\beta_2)$. The inverse: $F(\beta)=r$ for $r>0$ is equivalent to $(1-\beta)/(1+\beta)=r^2$, that is to $\beta(1+r^2)=1-r^2$, i.e. $\beta=\beta(r)$; this $\beta(r)$ lies in $(-1,1)$ because $|1-r^2|<1+r^2$, and the solution is unique by strict monotonicity. (b) Since $F$ is strictly decreasing with inverse $\beta(\cdot)$, $F(\beta)\in[z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon]$ is equivalent to $\beta\in[\beta(z+\varepsilon),\beta(z-\varepsilon)]$, and both endpoints lie in $(-1,1)$ because $z-\varepsilon>0$ makes $z+\varepsilon>0$; the declared box of the record is a closed interval in the value variable. At $\varepsilon=0$ both record endpoints equal z and the inverse produces the singleton $\{\beta(z)\}$. At $\varepsilon>0$, $z-\varepsilon<z+\varepsilon$ and the inverse is strictly decreasing, so the parameter endpoints are strictly ordered. Direct rational subtraction gives the displayed length $8z\varepsilon/[ (1+(z-\varepsilon)^2)(1+(z+\varepsilon)^2)]$, whose denominator is positive and whose numerator is positive exactly for positive uncertainty. (c) Substitute $r=91/100$ and $r=89/100$ into $\beta(r)$ and reduce: exact rational arithmetic; the length is $\beta(89/100)-\beta(91/100)$, computed by common denominators as $7200000/327613801>0$. The decimals are displayed to six places and are not used in any claim. No step uses a probability model, a sampling assumption or a measurement. The complete run configuration exists for every beta in (-1,1): the passive boost is proper orthochronous by lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse and thus yields an inertial boosted frame; choose the fixed covector with components (-omega/c,omega/c,0,0), future null by lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data(e). The two rest worldlines are straight future timelike histories of their respective frames. Their conditional frequency readings are supplied by the plane-wave postulate and Doppler theorem; the operational model introduces no claim that an apparatus realizes this configuration.

Step5a current-carrier reconciliation: Use the emitter h:R->A, h(rho)=o+rho e0, proper time rho/c, explicit affine phase and observer reception o; invoke Doppler(i),(ii).

It asserts no measurement, no statistical inference and no empirical conclusion about any model or postulate.
items.statement:
**Statement refuted.** A declared one-point data record of the vocabulary with positive declared uncertainty determines the parameter of an operational model uniquely: if a record R of clause (c) of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]] is consistent with two parameters $\beta_1,\beta_2$ of one operational model M, then $\beta_1=\beta_2$.

**Counterexample.** Adopt the SI convention $x^0=ct$ and the ideal plane-wave/frequency-reading model of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]], conditionally as in [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]]. Fix an inertial chart x and a positive angular frequency $\omega$. For every $\beta\in(-1,1)$ let $x'=B(\beta e_1)x$ be the passive boosted inertial chart; use an ideal emitter at rest in x, the future null wave covector with frame-x components $(-\omega/c,\omega/c,0,0)$ and propagation direction $s=e_1$, and the straight rest observer of x'. Let $S=\Theta=(-1,1)$, $\theta=\mathrm{id}$ and let $D(\beta)$ be this finite declared run description. The Doppler theorem gives $\omega_o=\gamma_\beta(1-\beta)\omega$, where $\gamma_\beta=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, so the dimensionless prediction is $$F(\beta)=\frac{\omega_o}{\omega}=\sqrt{\frac{1-\beta}{1+\beta}}.$$ Thus $M=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ satisfies the operational vocabulary's interpretation condition (*), with $d=1$; the interpretation is a conditional model computation, not an apparatus claim. Use the explicitly declared comparison rule that a parameter is consistent with a one-point scalar record exactly when its prediction lies in that record's declared closed interval.

Take the illustrative record $N=1$, $z_1=z=9/10$, $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon=1/100$ and annotation 'longitudinal Doppler ratio of the moving observer in the propagation direction'. These are declared illustrative values, not measurements. Its declared prediction interval is $[89/100,91/100]$. The map F is strictly decreasing on $(-1,1)$ and has inverse $\beta(r)=(1-r^2)/(1+r^2)$ for every $r>0$. Therefore the full consistency set is $$C(R,M)=\{\beta:F(\beta)\in[89/100,91/100]\}=[1719/18281,\,2079/17921].$$ In particular put $\beta_1=1719/18281$, $\beta_2=2079/17921$. Both are in $(-1,1)$ and $F(\beta_1)=91/100$, $F(\beta_2)=89/100$, hence both are consistent. Yet $$\beta_2-\beta_1=\frac{2079}{17921}-\frac{1719}{18281}=\frac{7200000}{327613801}>0,$$ with $17921\cdot18281=327613801$. This refutes uniqueness. In fact every parameter in that entire positive-length interval is consistent, including its endpoints. Nothing in this algebraic consistency rule supports the truth of M or of any physical postulate; no probability model, measurement, calibration, statistical inference or empirical conclusion is asserted.

For r>0, solving F(beta)=r is equivalent to 1-beta=r^2(1+beta), hence beta=(1-r^2)/(1+r^2). Its denominator is positive, and beta+1=2/(1+r^2)>0, 1-beta=2r^2/(1+r^2)>0, so the inverse lies in (-1,1).
